kicker: FIM · Historical Lorenz96 and delayed-recall study
title: Retained component ablations in a historical three-seed FIM evaluation
finding: Mean directions split 3–3 across six comparisons. The smallest exact sign-test p-value is 0.5.
main_caption: All paired removal-minus-full rollout-MSE differences are shown. Positive favors the full model; negative favors removal. The two benchmark panels have independent vertical scales.

columns.text: Two benchmarks × three seeds × four configurations give 24 retained cells. Configurations are full, no memory, no retrieval and no salience gating. The shared-minibatch protocol used 12 epochs, batch size 64 and four-step training versus 30-step evaluation rollouts.

All 96 text-artifact hashes were checked: a summary, run-results report, configuration and log for each cell. MSE and MAE agree across the retained reports and manifest. No checkpoint was read or replayed.
The largest mean full-model advantage, Lorenz96 salience gating, is driven by seed 23; the other two seeds favor removal. No-memory and no-retrieval error sequences coincide in both benchmarks.

The retained comparisons do not establish component necessity or a recovered memory mechanism. Matching error sequences do not prove prediction or implementation identity. Three seeds do not supply independent-domain replication.

With three nonzero pairs, the smallest possible two-sided exact sign-test p-value is 0.25; the observed minimum is 0.5. Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence. The executed Git revision is recorded as UNKNOWN, so full source reconstruction is not claimed.

This presentation covers the closed historical shared-minibatch study. Burgers V2, delayed-recall V2 and the held trajectory-isolated successor are separate projects. Their sources and outcomes are not substituted by this package.
